atoms.name: File organisations
atoms.one_line: Heap scans b/2 blocks, sorted binary-searches, hash jumps to one bucket; only ordered files serve ranges.

atoms.name: Index types
atoms.one_line: Primary: ordered key; clustering: ordered non-key; secondary: unordered; dense or sparse by entry count.

atoms.name: Blocking factors and index size
atoms.one_line: Records per block is a floor; blocks are a ceiling; index entries = key + pointer.

atoms.name: Index search cost
atoms.one_line: Binary search over index blocks costs ⌈log₂ b⌉; multi-level costs one access per level.

atoms.name: B and B+ tree order
atoms.one_line: Internal: p pointers, p−1 keys; leaf: pairs plus a next pointer; B-tree nodes carry data pointers too.

atoms.name: Height and node counts
atoms.one_line: Full nodes give minimum height, half-full nodes give maximum height; root needs only two children.

atoms.name: Insertion and splits
atoms.one_line: Leaf split copies up, internal split pushes up; a root split adds a level.

atoms.name: B-tree versus B+ tree
atoms.one_line: B+ keeps all data in linked leaves, so internal fan-out is higher; B-tree splits push keys out of leaves.

atoms.name: Choosing an index
atoms.one_line: Equality: hash or B+; range: ordered index; composite hash needs every column as equality.
